cond_0001.intro:
[Company name masked] is an independent, nonprofit organization providing adult cancer treatment and groundbreaking research focused on cancer and infectious diseases. [Company name masked] operates eight clinical care sites that provide medical oncology, infusion, radiation, proton therapy and related services, and network affiliations with hospitals in five states. Together, our fully integrated research and clinical care teams seek to discover new cures to the world's deadliest diseases and make life beyond cancer a reality.
The Rajan laboratory in the Basic Sciences Division at [Company name masked] uses multidisciplinary approaches to study dysfunctions in fat to brain communication underlies obesity. Our goal is to understand how fat communicates nutrient status to the brain, and how chronic nutrient surplus disrupts this communication. Examining this complex question in a simple model system, such as the fruit fly, will provide fundamental insights that can be leveraged to tackle obesity.
This is an ideal position for a recent graduate who wants to gain an intense research experience before pursuing graduate and/or medical school.
Additional information about the research in the Rajan lab can be found at: http://akhilalab.org
Cover letters are highly encouraged explaining your interested in the Rajan Lab.
cond_0001.responsibilities:
The Research Technician will primarily carry out an independent research project under direct supervision of a staff scientist that involves using in vitro cell culture systems including human primary cells, imaging, ELISA, biochemistry (western blots, immunoprecipitation) and molecular biology (cloning, PCR).
Other responsibilities include general lab maintenance (ordering, caring for Drosophila flies, fly media preparation), and other duties as needed.
cond_0001.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
BA/BS in a scientific field
Scientific knowledge in the area of study and basic laboratory skills
Good verbal and written communication skills
Good interpersonal skills and ability to be a strong team player
Scientific curiosity, self-motivation, and the ability to take instruction and correction and follow directions
Good organizational skills and the ability to work and think independently
Preferred Requirements
Independent research experience in addition to school lab experience
Willingness to stay at least two years

The Rajan laboratory in the Basic Sciences Division at [Company name masked] uses multidisciplinary approaches to study dysfunctions in fat to brain communication underlies obesity. cond_0449.intro:
[Company name masked] is an independent, nonprofit organization providing adult cancer treatment and groundbreaking research focused on cancer and infectious diseases. [Company name masked] operates eight clinical care sites that provide medical oncology, infusion, radiation, proton therapy and related services, and network affiliations with hospitals in five states. Together, our fully integrated research and clinical care teams seek to discover new cures to the world's deadliest diseases and make life beyond cancer a reality.
The Rajan laboratory in the Basic Sciences Division at [Company name masked] uses multidisciplinary approaches to study dysfunctions in fat to brain communication underlies obesity. Our goal is to understand how fat communicates nutrient status to the brain, and how chronic nutrient surplus disrupts this communication. Examining this complex question in a simple model system, such as the fruit fly, will provide fundamental insights that can be leveraged to tackle obesity.
This is an ideal position for a recent graduate who wants to gain an intense research experience before pursuing graduate and/or medical school.

[Company name masked] operates eight clinical care sites that provide medical oncology, infusion, radiation, proton therapy and related services, and network affiliations with hospitals in five states. Our fully integrated research and clinical care teams seek to discover new cures to the world's deadliest diseases and make life beyond cancer a reality.
The Rajan laboratory in the Basic Sciences Division at [Company name masked] uses multidisciplinary approaches to study dysfunctions in fat to brain communication that underlie obesity. Our goal is to understand how fat communicates nutrient status to the brain, and how chronic nutrient surplus disrupts this communication. Examining this complex question in a simple model system, such as the fruit fly, will provide fundamental insights that can be leveraged to tackle obesity.
This is an ideal position for a recent graduate who wants to gain an intense research experience before pursuing graduate and/or medical school.
Additional information about the research in the Rajan lab can be found at: http://akhilalab.org
Cover letters are highly encouraged explaining your interest in the Rajan Lab.
cond_0511.responsibilities:
The Research Technician will primarily carry out an independent research project under direct supervision of a staff scientist. The project involves in vitro cell culture systems including human primary cells, imaging, ELISA, biochemistry (western blots, immunoprecipitation), and molecular biology (cloning, PCR).
Other responsibilities include general lab maintenance (ordering, caring for Drosophila flies, fly media preparation), and other duties as needed.
cond_0511.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
BA/BS in a scientific field
Scientific knowledge in the area of study and basic laboratory skills
Reliability, self-motivation, and curiosity
Ability to take instruction and correction and follow directions
Good organizational skills and ability to work and think independently
Commitment to staying at least two years
Preferred Requirements
Independent research experience beyond school lab coursework
Good written communication skills and clear, direct verbal reporting
Ability to contribute constructively within a lab team
cond_0511.encouragement_text: Important: Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply.
cond_0511.workplace_support: We work to create an environment where employees feel supported, heard, and able to do their best work. Our approach includes flexibility, trust, and practical support that helps people thrive across changing needs and responsibilities.

cond_0525.intro:
We are looking for a Research Technician I to join our team.
The Rajan laboratory in the Basic Sciences Division at [Company name masked] uses multidisciplinary approaches to study dysfunctions in fat to brain communication underlies obesity. Our goal is to understand how fat communicates nutrient status to the brain, and how chronic nutrient surplus disrupts this communication. Examining this complex question in a simple model system, such as the fruit fly, will provide fundamental insights that can be leveraged to tackle obesity.
This is an ideal position for a recent graduate who wants to gain an intense research experience before pursuing graduate and/or medical school.
Additional information about the research in the Rajan lab can be found at: http://akhilalab.org
Cover letters are highly encouraged explaining your interested in the Rajan Lab.
cond_0525.responsibilities:
The Research Technician will primarily carry out an independent research project in a under direct supervision of a staff scientist that involves using in vitro cell culture systems including human primary cells, imaging, ELISA, biochemistry (western blots, immunoprecipitation) and molecular biology (cloning, PCR).
Other responsibilities include general lab maintenance (ordering, caring for Drosophila flies, fly media preparation), and other duties as needed.
cond_0525.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
BA/BS in a scientific field, or equivalent practical experience.
Working knowledge in the area of study and basic laboratory skills.
Ability to communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing.
Willingness to follow directions, take instruction and feedback, and stay organized.
Commitment to staying in the role for at least two years.
Preferred Requirements
Some independent research experience beyond standard coursework, though we consider relevant training and education.
Openness to learning and curiosity about the science — these go a long way in this role.
Comfort working both independently and as part of a team.
Good interpersonal skills and a collaborative approach.
